data_output.description: encode(splits) returns (encoded, dimension). encoded[split] remains a tuple (features, labels, users). features is an int32 matrix in exact column order [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, tab_hour], where tab_hour is the literal categorical tuple (tab, hour), tab is raw field tab, and hour is canonical floor(float(raw field hourmin)/100) constrained to 0..23. Each field, including tab_hour, has a vocabulary fitted on train rows only, one unknown ID, and a disjoint global offset. labels and users retain their existing types and row alignment; all split rows retain source order.

model_input.description: The unchanged Model accepts the encoded int32 feature matrix with six columns and computes bias plus the sum of the six corresponding categorical weights per row. The fixed unchanged training command must write predictions_valid.npz containing exactly row_ids and scores, with row_ids equal to sequential int64 validation row indices and scores in canonical validation row order; validation ground truth remains external to the prediction artifact and is loaded only by the fixed evaluator.

feature_engineer.objective: Implement exactly one additional train-vocabulary categorical interaction feature, tab_hour, in data.py so the existing additive scorer receives user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, and tab_hour.
required_changes: In data.py, change FIELDS from ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour", "weekday"] to ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour", "weekday", "tab_hour"].

Keep the existing canonical hour derivation exactly as integer hour = floor(numeric raw field hourmin / 100), validate it is in 0..23, and continue deriving weekday from raw field date as Monday=0 through Sunday=6.

In encode(), extend raw(row) to return the five existing values followed by the categorical tuple (row[3], row[4]), where row[3] is raw field tab and row[4] is the already canonically derived hour. Do not stringify, hash, bucket, or otherwise transform either component.

Build the tab_hour vocabulary solely by iterating training rows through the same existing vocabulary-building loop. Reserve exactly one unknown ID for tab_hour exactly as for every other field, and map validation/test tab_hour tuples absent from the training vocabulary to that field's unknown ID.

Retain the existing global offset construction, int32 feature matrix encoding, labels, users, split date filtering, source-file iteration order, and per-split row order. The resulting encoded feature matrices must have six columns in FIELDS order and dimension must remain the sum of all six vocabulary dimensions.
preserve: Do not add any raw source column, joined source, target-derived feature, aggregate, or feature beyond tab_hour.
Use only eligible raw field tab and the canonical hour derived from eligible raw field hourmin; do not use time_ms, long_view as an input, any forbidden outcome field, or any quarantined statistic.

Do not modify model.py, train.py, or config.json. The model architecture remains the existing additive weight sum and all loss, optimizer, regularization, seed, and schedule settings remain unchanged.

Preserve canonical validation source row order so the unchanged training command emits predictions_valid.npz with row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels), dtype=np.int64) and scores aligned to that validation order.
coordination_notes: The unchanged Model.logits sums one weight per encoded feature column, so the sixth tab_hour column automatically adds exactly one additive categorical term without a model.py change.
The unchanged train.py contract probe derives its displayed feature shape from train_features and therefore should report six feature columns after this edit.
No config edit is required; trainer must not be activated.

reasoning: The hypothesis is a features-only ablation: add one categorical conjunction of eligible raw tab and canonically derived hour while preserving the existing additive model and all training settings. data.py is the sole owned file requiring a change. A training-only tuple vocabulary with a reserved unknown value prevents validation/test vocabulary leakage and preserves the fixed prediction interface.
